predecessors.name: Tang dynasty
predecessors.text: Liu Yin's Guangzhou command, named regional governor and military officer by the Tang court in 905: the south coast of Guangdong and Guangxi

successors.name: Song dynasty (Northern and Southern Song)
successors.text: present-day Guangdong province (Song conquest page), with Guangxi and Hainan: the whole Southern Han realm

ledger.x: 907: the Tang falls and Liu Yin keeps the south coast.
908: Ma Yin takes six prefectures from Liu Yin.
917: Liu Yan proclaims a kingdom, Yue.
931: Duong Dinh Nghe drives the Han out.
951: Liu Sheng seizes Lingnan from the fallen Chu.
971: the Song take Guangzhou and end the Southern Han.

wars.name: Ma Chu campaign against Liu Yin
wars.outcome: Ma Yin took six prefectures (Zhao, He, Wu, Meng, Gong, Fu) in 908; Liu Yin took Rong and Gao in 911 after Ma's man Yao Yanzhang withdrew; Emperor Taizu brokered peace in 911 and Liu Yan married into the Ma family in 913-915.

wars.name: Southern Han invasions of Jinghai
wars.outcome: Taken in October 930 and lost in 931; in late 938 the Han fleet under Liu Hongcao met Ngo Quyen's at the Bach Dang River and 'half of the Han army died, either killed or drowned, including Liu Hongcao'; Liu Yan turned back to Guangzhou and Ngo Quyen…

wars.name: Southern Han invasion of Chu
wars.outcome: Southern Han occupied Lingnan land of the fallen Chu in winter 951 and held it against a failed Southern Tang counterattack.

wars.name: Song conquest of Southern Han
wars.outcome: Song forces captured Guangzhou in 971 and annexed the Southern Han; its emperor Liu Chang surrendered.

certainty.note: Coastal Guangdong and Guangxi are described by prefectures; no treaty line exists.
